Areas of Focus

My work sits where traditional philanthropic values meet modern institutional systems: trust, resources, people, technology, and measurable impact. An institution's success is not how much it raises, but how well it converts generosity into lasting change.

Humanitarian Field Deployment

Indonesian Delegation, Gaza Relief Mission

Arab Republic of Egypt · 13–21 August 2026

Represented the institution as one of fourteen Indonesian non-governmental organisations deployed under the Konsorsium Kebaikan Indonesia Hadiah untuk Palestina initiative, accompanying the dispatch of 5,067 food packages in six container trucks from Egypt into Gaza.

Coordinated with consortium partners and in-country counterparts on cross-border delivery logistics, beneficiary verification and accountability of donated goods.

Engaged directly with displaced Palestinian communities in Egypt through food assistance, psychosocial programming for children, Qur'an education for hafiz students, and a visit to the Palestinian hospital treating casualties evacuated from Gaza.

Presence is a form of aid. Witness is a form of responsibility. Solidarity is what keeps a humanitarian movement alive.

Projects

Four bodies of work — with the numbers, and with what did not go to plan.

Project 1

Egypt–Palestine Humanitarian Mission

Cross-border humanitarian action · August 2026

The context. We were not only meeting material need; we were meeting people carrying loss, trauma, displacement and an unresolved future. The challenge was keeping assistance both relevant and dignified, and making sure attention to Gaza did not end when the news cycle moved on.

What I learned. Humanitarian response is not only distribution. It is presence, listening, keeping hope alive, building networks, and making sure the voices of those affected do not disappear from public attention. Good intentions are not the same as effective intervention — we must listen more than we assume.

What I would change. Stronger needs assessment before intervening; monitoring that measures what changed for people rather than what was delivered; and an integrated strategy connecting relief, psychosocial support, spiritual support and long-term advocacy.

Project 2

Digital Fundraising Academy

Founder and Chief Executive Officer · 2025–present

The problem. Indonesian zakat institutions, waqf boards and mosque committees were being told to go digital without being given the professional foundations to do it. Training in the sector tended to stop at the seminar — a day of inspiration, no follow-through, no change in how the institution actually ran.

What I built. Capacity-building programmes covering professional governance, programme utilisation, sustainability and fundraising management, delivered through webinars, seminars, bootcamps and in-house training — then continued as institutional consultancy and long-term mentoring rather than ending at the certificate.

Outcome. More than a thousand cumulative participants, including mosque administrators and philanthropy practitioners across Indonesia. Consultancy engagements followed with Satu Amal Indonesia, Rumah Quran Rabbani and Rabithah Peduli, extending into organisational structure, SOPs, core team formation and donor network strategy.

Project 3

A National Philanthropy Network of 98 Branches

Director of Philanthropy Network · 2017–2022

The problem. A national network is only as strong as its weakest branch. Retail fundraising sat well below its potential, and branches were working against targets without shared channels or a common way of engaging donors.

What I did. Led the network against fundraising and programme impact targets, and developed seven distinct philanthropy channels so branches had more than one route to the donor — much of it branch by branch, mapping donor bases and rebuilding approaches from the ground up.

Outcome. Branch retail fundraising rose to 40 per cent of the national total and retail donor engagement increased by 65 per cent. The seven-channel structure gave branches a repeatable method rather than a target to improvise against.

Project 4

Building a Volunteer Ecosystem

Secretary General, Masyarakat Relawan Indonesia · 2020–2024

The problem. Volunteer movements grow fast and organise slowly. Numbers alone do not make a network deployable — without structure, a large volunteer base cannot be matched to the work that actually needs doing.

What I built. Alongside growing the network across 38 provinces and 390 districts and cities, I established a volunteer clustering system organised by programme area and by profession, so that skills could be matched to need rather than counted in aggregate.

Outcome. A national volunteer society of 81,499 members with a structure that made specialised deployment possible, supported by disaster preparedness training that prepares people for the role they will actually hold.

Case study

Contested Legitimacy in Indonesian Zakat Governance

Twelve data sources · three practitioner interviews · one constitutional challenge

A qualitative study of state–private competition in Indonesian zakat, arguing that what is really contested is legitimacy — and introducing digital legitimacy as credibility earned through real-time transparency rather than conferred by legal status.
